prompt: One naturalistic 1:1 SQUARE winter allotment photo for the second page-151 inset in The Vegetable Guru. Revise image 1, the December Cavolo Nero in John's exact bed, correcting placement and clarity of the BRICK FOOTPATHS. This time COMPOSE AS A SQUARE with slightly wider horizontal field of view than the prior tight crop. Preserve the site as shown in image 2, the authentic wide May photograph, and image 3, the August ground-level path in the same view. The 4th image is the actual overhead site plan evidence: two narrow paved strips run along the long edges of the same rectangular bean/kale bed, one nearer the camera and one behind the row. They connect at the right (shed end) into the area of larger 45 cm square paving slabs. They do not surround or retain the soil or turn the left grass margin into pavers. Use this geometry, not the printed annotations or the plants in the aerial views. Main correction: make the authentic foreground walkway clearly visible INSIDE the finished square. It is a NARROW, roughly two-small-bricks-wide, near-flush light brown/grey worn rectangular brick/paver strip with real irregular joint lines and moist dark patches, running DIAGONALLY from about 60–66 percent across the BOTTOM edge towards the right edge near the shed end, on the right/near side of the bed exactly as images 2 and 3 show. Show it continuously for enough of the right foreground that the way to the square slabs by the shed is apparent. Do not place the entire strip off the right edge. The farther parallel cross-strip on the back long edge should be glimpsed in short visible portions separating cleared beds and leading to the same paving junction, in correct perspective and partly occluded behind the kale. All paths are at ground level, narrow and weathered, not oversized patios, timber edges, new curbs or rectangular borders all around. Hold the authentic left west wall below its conifer overhang and left slate roof, grass on the left, distant right hedge separate, and the pale green shed edge on the right if within this near-matching field of view. No invented water butt, shed or extended rear wall. Retain the earlier December scene and natural plant character: three to four distinct Cavolo Nero plants in the actual bean bed, an uneven near crown with overlapping matte blue-green leaves, a few harvest scars lower down, a little yellowing on one outer leaf and only sparse small incidental insect holes. Keep the plants a clear foreground subject inside the square with enough context, no perfect cloned fans. ALL background vegetable crops are already harvested; leave mostly bare damp soil beside and behind, a few little cut stalks, the actual grass margins and unobtrusive low empty hoops as supported by original sources. All bean canes removed. Soft neutral overcast early-winter light and damp paving, no snow, no people, no type. This must be a seamless edge-to-edge SQUARE photo from near the familiar camera viewpoint, with the brick strips visibly preserved.
